newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ to fight continued Australian ban on NZ apples.
newsitem.headline: NZ to fight continued Australian ban on NZ apples.

text.p: New Zealand vowed on Monday to fight an Australian draft decision to continue a ban on importing New Zealand apples.
International Trade Minister Lockwood Smith called an Australian Quarantine Inspection Service (AQIS) draft recommendation to retain the ban "extremely disappointing".
He said that with a potential market worth millions of dollars at stake, New Zealand would continue to fight for access to Australia.
A final decision on the issue will be made after June 13, following public consultations. Smith said New Zealand's case remained very strong.
"I am confident that our position can withstand international scrutiny. We hope to persuade AQIS to reconsider its position."

Australia has banned imports of New Zealand apples for decades because of fears they might introduce the potentially devastating disease fire blight. New Zealand has been pushing for access since the 1920s.
It reapplied for access after the the international agreement on sanitary and phytosanitary measures came into effect in 1994. That agreement states bans must be on good scientific grounds.
The AQIS said earlier on Monday it was not satisfied with New Zealand research that had found fire blight absent from New Zealand apples.
The New Zealand researchers had not conducted their study under the same conditions that would apply to proposed exports, the service said, reporting on its own investigation.
New Zealand Apple and Pear Marketing Board chairman John McCliskie said New Zealand growers would be bitterly disappointed the Australian government had decided to continue its ban.

"We were hoping the draft import risk assessment would accept the New Zealand case that mature apples are not a vector (carrier) for fire blight. Our case is sound and reflects New Zealand's position in other important offshore markets.

"We will now work with the government to determine the next steps. We regard access to the Australian market as an important case, not only for growers, but for all New Zealand's exporting links with Australia under CER."
McCliskie said the board will argue New Zealand's case strongly in Australia.
Australian quarantine regulations currently prohibit imports of fresh apples, although trade in processed apple products has been reasonably free of regulation.

Australia is free of fire blight but the AQIS said it was uncertain how the disease was transmitted through apple trade. "The New Zealand claim that apples cannot act as a vector for fire blight is unproven," it said, adding that the New Zealand export proposal did not provide enough quarantine safeguards.
"On the basis of these findings, AQIS (foreshadows) rejecting the New Zealand proposal," it said in a statement.
